title: Nasal [ɑ̃] — an, am, en, em (set 4)
focus: These spellings all make the nasal vowel [ɑ̃], as in « enfant ». In Québec it is usually pronounced further forward in the mouth than in Paris, so it can sound close to a Parisian « in » — listen for that. Careful: the verb ending -ent (« ils chantent ») is silent, never nasal, and a following vowel or doubled n/m cancels the nasal (« banane », « Jeanne »). « chemise » isn't nasal: a vowel follows the m.

sentences.fr: Samedi, j'aime magasiner avec ma t[an]te.
sentences.en: On Saturday, I like to go shopping with my aunt.

sentences.fr: Nous cherchons un p[an]talon et une chemise bl[an]che.
sentences.en: We're looking for pants and a white shirt.

sentences.fr: Ma t[an]te trouve ça trop cher, alors nous [en]trons d[an]s un autre magasin.
sentences.en: My aunt thinks it's too expensive, so we go into another store.
